title: Friday Sermon 59 by Dean Mahmoud: Adam and Eve's Garments, Bodies, and Temptation (1982-11-19)

cases.question: What did the original garment symbolize?
cases.expected_answer_note: Dean reviews Quran 20:118 and 7:22–27. Adam and Eve did not hunger or go naked in the garden. Their original covering may symbolize natural obedience, Satan's temptation stripped that obedience, and later scripture promises Adam's descendants a better garment of righteousness.

cases.question: How did the garment of righteousness differ?
cases.expected_answer_note: Dean reviews Quran 20:118 and 7:22–27. Adam and Eve did not hunger or go naked in the garden. Their original covering may symbolize natural obedience, Satan's temptation stripped that obedience, and later scripture promises Adam's descendants a better garment of righteousness.

cases.question: What methodological distinction did Dean make?
cases.expected_answer_note: Dean compares translations of Quran 7:27 that say bodies, nakedness, shame, or shameful parts. He distinguishes factual description from moral evaluation and suspects that some shame language entered through influence from the Hebrew Bible.

cases.question: Why did he prefer body or nakedness over shameful parts?
cases.expected_answer_note: Dean compares translations of Quran 7:27 that say bodies, nakedness, shame, or shameful parts. He distinguishes factual description from moral evaluation and suspects that some shame language entered through influence from the Hebrew Bible.

cases.question: What two temptations were compared?
cases.expected_answer_note: Dean compares Quran 7:20 and 20:120. Satan promises that the tree will make Adam and Eve angels or immortals and offers the tree of eternity and everlasting kingship. The sermon analyzes Arabic roots connected with whispering, angel or king, and eternity.

cases.question: Which Arabic roots linked angels or kingship and eternity?
cases.expected_answer_note: Dean compares Quran 7:20 and 20:120. Satan promises that the tree will make Adam and Eve angels or immortals and offers the tree of eternity and everlasting kingship. The sermon analyzes Arabic roots connected with whispering, angel or king, and eternity.

cases.question: What did Adam and Eve fail to become?
cases.expected_answer_note: Dean argues that Adam and Eve were always intended to be mortal beings of Earth and that Satan deceived them because neither immortality nor angelhood followed. He compares their expulsion with students failing an early term of training and says they then recognized bodies limited by space, time, flesh, blood, and mortality.
